title: Ransomware containment chain without Microsoft 365
use_case: On a Critical ransomware or hands-on-keyboard detection in a tenant without Microsoft 365, isolate the host, turn on Adaptive Attack Protection for it and its device group, block the file hash, collect forensic logs, page on-call and comment a timeline on the case.
trigger: Platform Events, source Alert2 (detections), event create, with the Only When filter in SETUP.md. Or User Initiated, a Response Action on Case, to run it by hand from a case.
connections: Taegis.SophosEndpoint 1.3.4, the Sophos Endpoint connector Sophos manages, to isolate, turn on Adaptive Attack Protection, block hashes and request forensic logs
Taegis.Case 1.0.5 and Taegis.Alert 1.3.6, the case and detection connectors Sophos manages, to read detections and comment the timeline
The Send Notification Message interface, set to Sophos's Teams, Slack or Google Chat template and a webhook connection, to page on-call
requires: Sophos Endpoint devices, Teams, Slack or Google Chat, an S3 bucket for forensic snapshots for the forensic step, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and Sophos MDR may already be containing the same host. A run from a case acts only on self-managed cases unless you turn on Include Sophos-managed cases. The detection trigger doesn't check who works the detection, so agree it with the Sophos MDR team first.
rollback: Release each device with Restore Host, turn Adaptive Attack Protection off or let it expire after 24 hours, and remove the blocked hashes from Blocked Items.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook is the Ransomware containment chain without its Microsoft 365 user step: on a Critical ransomware or hands-on-keyboard detection it isolates the host, turns on Adaptive Attack Protection for it and its device group, blocks the file hash, collects forensic logs, pages on-call and comments a timeline on the case. It needs no Microsoft Graph API connection. Dry run is on.
notes:
Setup:
- It's Ransomware containment chain without the user step and Ask for approval first, so it needs no Microsoft Graph API connection. Sophos Fusion won't save a configured playbook without a connection for every connector its template lists.
- Forensic logs need an AWS S3 bucket set up for forensic snapshots, Windows devices and an XDR or MDR license. Without the bucket Sophos answers "Upload disabled", so turn the step off.

How it works:
- Its tasks are the Microsoft 365 version's, less the user step; a repo test keeps them identical.
- It never blocks the hashes of a detection that names a file on Never block or under Windows\System32 or SysWOW64: those often carry the hash of powershell.exe or cmd.exe.

Testing:
- On 2026-11-16 the dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in us01 and eu02, and a renamed copy imported, exported (same apart from whitespace and connector order) and was deleted in eu02.
- In us01 a renamed copy, configured with no Microsoft Graph API connection, ran in dry run on a test case and live on an offline test device: Adaptive Attack Protection on the device and its group and the hash block were read back and reverted, and the Teams page posted. No log held a secret.

Known gaps:
- Isolation never ran: no test device was online. Forensic logs only reached Sophos's Upload disabled answer: the test tenant has no S3 bucket.
- No real ransomware or hands-on-keyboard detection was used, and the case menu run wasn't tested.
